content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur on the face, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a head horn grown from the frontal bone of the head, above and between the eyes, out of the covering, which continues from there into the body covering of smooth, glossy dark cuticle, one long curved head horn curving upward and back from the head; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the brown bear's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs and tail. It replaces the brown bear's dense fur there and conforms to the brown bear's body, a few large, smooth, fused plates, each spanning a whole body region of the brown bear (the shoulders, the back, the hips, each limb section), sized to the brown bear's body, joined by flexible cuticle at every joint; every covered part keeps the brown bear's own length and shape, and the tail stays the brown bear's own tail; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face keeps the brown bear's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and rows of small breathing openings (spiracles) along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature image**
I'm planning a single creature with a brown bear's four-legged silhouette and head, adding the European rhinoceros beetle's frontal horn and smooth glossy body covering over the bear's dense fur and plain coat.
**Reviewing beetle reference details**
I'm checking reference details for a European rhinoceros beetle to guide the chitin plates, horn curve, and spiracles before drafting the illustration.
**Composing hybrid creature image**
I'm building the hybrid illustration using the bear head with fur and eyes, plus chitin plates, a head horn, glossy dark cuticle, and spiracles along the flanks, set in a natural history style with a plain light background in a 1:1 frame.
**Refining hybrid creature design**
I'm generating another version to better integrate the elements and make the creature look more realistic, with less armor-like detailing and natural spiracles.
**Selecting final creature image**
I'm choosing media_4h8nyl as the final version because it looks more integrated with a lighter belly and visible spiracles, and I'm noting it as the best option to use.
